## 4.2 Descriptive summaries and graphs
#Summarize the dataset by Continent
```{r}
continent_summary <- Happiness_corruption %>%
  group_by(continent) %>%
  summarise(Observations = n(),
            Mean_Happiness = mean(happiness_score, na.rm = TRUE),
            Mean_CPI = mean(cpi_score, na.rm = TRUE),
            Mean_GDP = mean(gdp_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Observations))

print(continent_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Summary statistics by continent")

ggplot(continent_summary,
       aes(x = reorder(continent, Mean_Happiness), y = Mean_Happiness)) +
  geom_col(fill = "blue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Average happiness score by continent",
       x = "Continent", y = "Average happiness score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Summary by year
```{r}
year_summary <-Happiness_corruption %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(Observations = n(),
            Mean_Happiness = mean(happiness_score, na.rm = TRUE),
            Mean_CPI = mean(cpi_score, na.rm = TRUE),
            Mean_GDP = mean(gdp_per_capita, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

print(year_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Summary statistics by year")
ggplot(year_summary, aes(x = Year, y = Mean_Happiness)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(size = 2, colour = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(Happiness_corruption$Year))) +
  labs(title = "Global average happiness score, 2015–2020",
       x = "Year", y = "Average happiness score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Happiness Score, CPI Score and GDP per Capita.
```{r}
p1 <- ggplot(Happiness_corruption , aes(x = happiness_score)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "blue", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of happiness scores",
       x = "Happiness score", y = "Number of observations") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(Happiness_corruption , aes(x = cpi_score)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 0,
                 fill = "green", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of CPI scores",
       x = "CPI score", y = "Number of observations") +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(Happiness_corruption , aes(x = gdp_per_capita)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "orange", colour = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of GDP per capita",
       x = "GDP per capita", y = "Number of observations") +
  theme_minimal()
p1
p2
p3
```
The EDA shows that . . . 28.79. . . . . % of the observations come from European coun-
tries. Moreover, . . . .248 . . . . out of all country–year observations have a CPI score

of 50 or above. In addition, the average happiness score of Europe is . .1.42 . . . . . .

times the average happiness score of Africa. Generally, the global average happi-
ness score moved from . . . 5.4375. . . . . in 2015 to . . . . .5.5599 . . . in 2020.

##4.3 How does the happiness score vary by continent,year,and by CPI score group
#How does the happiness score vary by continent
```{r}
ggplot(Happiness_corruption, aes(x = continent, y = happiness_score, fill = continent)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Happiness score distribution by continent",
       x = "Continent", y = "Happiness score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))


```
#How does the happiness score vary by year
```{r}
ggplot(Happiness_corruption, aes(x = factor(Year), y = happiness_score,
                 group = Year)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(title = "Happiness score distribution by year",
       x = "Year", y = "Happiness score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#How does the happiness score vary by CPI score group
```{r}
 Happiness_corruption<- Happiness_corruption %>%
  mutate(CPI_Group = cut(cpi_score,
                        breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 10),
                        right = FALSE,
                        include.lowest = TRUE,
                        labels = paste(seq(0, 90, 10),
                                       seq(9, 99, 10), sep = "–")))

cpi_group_summary <- Happiness_corruption %>%
  group_by(CPI_Group) %>%
  summarise(Observations = n(),
            Mean_Happiness = mean(happiness_score, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

print(cpi_group_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = "Average happiness by CPI interval")

ggplot(cpi_group_summary,
       aes(x = CPI_Group, y = Mean_Happiness, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2, colour = "yellow") +
  labs(title = "Average happiness by CPI score group",
       x = "CPI score interval", y = "Average happiness score") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Scatter plot and correlation between CPI and happiness

```{r cpi-correlation}
ggplot(Happiness_corruption, aes(x = cpi_score, y = happiness_score)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "darkred") +
  labs(title = "Relationship between CPI and happiness",
       x = "CPI score (higher means less perceived corruption)",
       y = "Happiness score") +
  theme_minimal()

cpi_happiness_correlation <- cor(Happiness_corruption$cpi_score,
                                 Happiness_corruption$happiness_score,
                                 use = "complete.obs",
                                 method = "pearson")
cpi_happiness_correlation
```

#4.4Identify one group of countries with a notably low happiness level.
```{r}
low_group <-Happiness_corruption %>%
  filter(continent == "Africa", cpi_score < 30)

low_group_countries <- sort(unique(low_group$Country))
low_group_mean <- mean(low_group$happiness_score, na.rm = TRUE)
global_mean <- mean(Happiness_corruption$happiness_score, na.rm = TRUE)
difference <- low_group_mean - global_mean
percent_below <- 100 * (global_mean - low_group_mean) / global_mean

print(low_group %>%
        group_by(Country) %>%
        summarise(Observations = n(),
                  Average_Happiness = mean(happiness_score),
                  Average_CPI = mean(cpi_score),
                  .groups = "drop") %>%
        arrange(Average_Happiness),
      digits = 3,
      caption = "Countries in the selected low-happiness group")

cat("Number of country-year observations:", nrow(low_group), "\n")
cat("Number of distinct countries:", length(low_group_countries), "\n")
cat("Countries:", paste(low_group_countries, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Group average happiness:", round(low_group_mean, 3), "\n")
cat("Global average happiness:", round(global_mean, 3), "\n")
cat("Difference (group minus global):", round(difference, 3), "\n")
cat("Group average is", round(percent_below, 1),
    "% below the global average.\n")
```


#4.5 Provide five practical recommendations for policymakers who want to improve
#citizenswell-being, based on your analysis.  ́

1.Prioritise countries and communities facing observations with CPI below 30 because they have a lower average happiness score than the global average.

2.Policymakers should protect civil rights, improve
   access to information and create meaningful opportunities for citizens to
   participate in decisions that affect them(personal freedom)
   
3.Promote transparent and accountable institutions
4.Improve public health and access to healthcare
5.Strengthen economic opportunity
